What happened

Every test ever run, and whether the ideas actually complement each other or just repeat the same bet in different clothing.

Do they work together?Every test run
These numbers are from a simulated market, not the real one. The system has been built and audited, but the study against real market prices has not run yet. Everything here demonstrates that the machinery works — none of it says anything about how these ideas would have actually performed.

Do these ideas work well together?

Two mediocre strategies can beat a good one if they fail at different times. This checks whether they actually do.

Does anything here actually behave differently?

The most useful result of the previous round was a negative one: nearly every idea tested turned out to be the same bet in different clothing. Two new families were added to attack that directly. This is whether they worked.

Yes — but only by not being permanently long. The hedged and market-neutral strategies sit at a median correlation of -0.05. The best long-only family manages 0.63, and most are far higher.

That gap is the whole finding, and it is not subtle. Every earlier attempt to find something “different” kept the long-only constraint, so the co-movement it was trying to escape was built into it. Nothing about technology stocks was ever the cause. The cost is real: a hedged book pays borrow every day, trades two sides instead of one, and gives up most of the raw return — check it against the benchmarks before treating low correlation as a good thing on its own.

How closely do they move together?

1.00 means two strategies rise and fall in lockstep — holding both gives you no protection. Lower numbers mean they behave differently, which is what makes combining them worthwhile. Darker = moves together.

Every test run

One row per run. Nothing is ever deleted — failures and retired ideas stay here permanently, which is what stops the same dead end being explored twice.

1699 registry records — nothing is ever deleted. The universe column says which roster of companies each run saw. Superseded runs were made against an earlier, narrower list; they are kept for the record and excluded from every ranking and comparison on this site, because a score earned picking among 33 megacaps means something different from one earned picking among 120 companies.
